CONFIDENTIAL
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
S.I. Special Branch.
REPORT
Date June 28, 19 38.

Subject Kiangwan Race Course - proposed sale.

Made by D.S. Hide Forwarded by [Signature]

The prospective purchaser of the International
Recreation Club's Kiangwan Race Course is reported to be
a Japanese citizen who arrived in Shanghai from Tokyo about
two months ago. Particulars regarding his identity are
not yet available but it is reliably stated that he has
no connection with Japanese officialdom and is acting on
behalf of private interests only.

He approached the Shanghai Race Club, which has
a predominant interest in the International Recreation
Club, offering to purchase the Kiangwan Race Course for
$800,000.00 less 5%.

Despite opposition emanating from Chinese members
who voiced apprehension regarding the motive of purchase,
this offer was accepted by a vote of 21 to 10 at a meeting
of the Shanghai Race Club on June 13th, 1938.

The Japanese was notified of this decision and
completion of the sale is now awaited in the form of
payment in two installments of $400,000.00 less 5 %.

Having due regard for the present condition of
the Race Course the deal is considered very satisfactory
and an excellent opportunity to liquidate a mortgage of
some $500,000.00 held by the Hongkong and Shanghai Banking
Corporation. In this connection however, it has been
definitely ascertained that the Bank has not pressed for
settlement.

The prospective purchaser has expressed his intention
of reconstructing the Race Course for the purpose of con-
tinuing racing under private management. He has undertaken
that meetings will not clash with those conducted by the

特别股。
报告
日期：1938年6月28日。

主题：江湾跑马厅——拟议出售事宜。

呈报人：D.S. Hide 转呈人：[签名]

据报，国际娱乐总会（International Recreation Club）江湾跑马厅的意向购买者是一名日本公民，约两个月前从东京抵达上海。关于其身份的具体细节尚不可得，但有可靠消息称，他与日本官方没有任何关联，仅代表私人利益行事。

他接触了在国际娱乐总会中占主导利益的上海跑马总会，提出以800,000.00美元减去5%的价格购买江湾跑马厅。

尽管来自华人会员的反对声音表达了对购买动机的担忧，但在1938年6月13日举行的上海跑马总会会议上，该提议仍以21票对10票获得通过。

该日本人已获知此决定，目前正等待交易完成，付款方式为两期付款，每期400,000.00美元减去5%。

鉴于跑马厅目前的状况，这笔交易被认为非常令人满意，并且是清偿汇丰银行所持约500,000.00美元抵押贷款的绝佳机会。然而，在此方面已确切查明，银行并未催促结算。

意向购买者已表示打算重建跑马厅，以便在私人管理下继续举办赛马活动。他承诺，赛马日程不会与上海跑马总会及中国赛马会举办的赛事冲突，且他已请求后者的友好合作。

（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处 / 1938年6月28日 / 通讯）

SALE OF I.R.C.
Editor, THE SHANGHAI TIMES
Sir,—Your issue of June 24 contains a letter from Mr. Yu Ya-ching enclosing the text of a letter addressed by him to the Chairman of the General Committee of the International Recreation Club.
Inter alia this states that:—
“... unknown to the Chairman and Committee of the International Recreation Club, the Stewards of the Shanghai Race Club had been negotiating for the sale of the property to Japanese buyers, and this only became known to the Chairman and Committee of the International Recreation Club at a Committee Meeting held on May 25.”
I am directed by the Stewards of the Shanghai Race Club to inform you that this statement is entirely untrue. The only offer for the purchase of the property was received on the morning of May 25 and this was immediately communicated to the General Committee of the International Recreation Club at a special meeting convened on the same day for that purpose. Mr. Yu Ya-ching was himself present at that meeting and must be fully aware of the circumstances.
I am directed to ask you to be good enough to publish this letter in your next issue.
A. W. OLSEN,
Secretary.
Shanghai Race Club
Shanghai, June 24, 1938.

DS Kua
6 5/6

我受上海跑马总会董事局指示通知您，此陈述完全不实。唯一的购买要约是在5月25日上午收到的，并于同日为此目的召开的特别会议上立即通报给国际娱乐总会总委员会。余亚庆先生本人出席了那次会议，必然充分知晓相关情况。

A. W. OLSEN，

Kiangwan Race Track
Sale Stated Blunder

It need no longer be disguised that the strongest of feelings were recently provoked in and outside the I.R.C. as well as the Shanghai Race Club as emphatic protests against the proposed sale of the Kiangwan Racecourse—the only Chinese sporting institution remaining in this district—and particularly was this resentment directed against the hurried and immediate transfer of this fine area of levelled ground of 1160 mow to the Japanese military authorities, at this political stage. It was no compassionate gesture to make to our Chinese hosts.

Distorted Versions
Various distorted versions have crept on to the pages of the local papers, but none of the critics made an effort to reflect the indignation which has been seething in genuine sporting circles. The abandonment of the mortgaged tract of land and building might have been prompted or fostered by gentlemen who were convinced that Shanghai could no longer maintain two sporting centers, that the economic situation called for an early revision of outlook, that a financial burden might be lifted if the present opportunity were seized, and the bogey of possible (not probable) confiscation of valuable property be laid forever. Philanthropic motives were never attributed to the parties concerned.

Cold Blooded Business
It was a cold-blooded business deal, with cash at the close of it. This is an utilitarian age. Everything is transmuted to chilled cash. Traditions are no longer hallowed. The labors of pioneers do not command reverence.
Indeed, if a light were shed on the diligent manner in which this sale scheme was promoted a tribute would be paid to the Chinese gentleman and true sportsman who had been quietly invited to second the resolution endorsing the sale, but who had the courage to definitely decline at the meeting of club members to fulfil his part because he had been belatedly enlightened as to the nationality of the purchasers, and his conscience revolted against the thought of a great sports ground being desecrated.

Another Thing
Then there was the sporting stalwart of considerable influence who insisted, in writing, that the stewards of the Shanghai Race Club should advise the Consular authorities of the proposed transfer before official action had been belatedly enlightened as to the approved by interested members, &c., and if this request was not complied with he would not hesitate to do so.
But, it appears now that the transfer is, unfortunately, on its way to completion, the mortgage will be liquidated, and all parties chuckling with contentment save that body of sportsmen who feel that they have had their birthright sold for a mess of pottage, are now denied that fine institution of which they had been so proud for years, and are convinced that once more in Shanghai we have seen how—even in sporting circles—turgid tyranny can suppress the aspirations and convictions of a solid and vociferous minority. The figure quoted as payment has varied from a million dollars to eight lacs. One local critic asserted that about six lacs were due to the Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation.

A Sure Sign
That which has been forgotten by the public is the fact that an area of 1160 mow of land is to be utilised as an airdrome by the Japanese, a sure sign of permanent occupation of large tracts of land in China. Then there are two roads, which were made by the I.R.C. on land acquired by the I.R.C., asphalted, and made over to the Chinese authorities some years ago.
The community regrets the hurried disposal of a great lung, and sportsmen deplore the lack of perspicacity on the part of their philanthropic brethren.

D. J. Hau
Rat

江湾跑马厅
出售被称为失策

无需再掩饰的是，最近在国际娱乐总会内部及外部，以及上海跑马总会内部，都引发了强烈的情绪，人们强烈抗议拟议出售江湾跑马厅——这是该地区仅存的中国体育机构——特别是这种愤慨指向在此政治阶段将该片1160亩平整的优质土地匆忙并立即移交给日本军方当局。这对我们的中国东道主而言，绝非一种充满同情心的姿态。

歪曲的版本
各种歪曲的说法已潜入当地报纸的版面，但没有任何评论员努力反映真正体育界中沸腾的愤怒。放弃这片抵押的土地和建筑，可能是由那些确信上海无法再维持两个体育中心、认为经济形势要求尽早修正观念、认为若抓住当前机会可减轻财务负担、并永远消除有价值财产可能被（并非很可能）没收的梦魇的绅士们所推动或助长的。从未有人将慈善动机归因于有关各方。

冷酷的商业交易
这是一笔冷酷的商业交易，最终以现金收场。这是一个功利主义的时代。一切都被转化为冰冷的现金。传统不再神圣。先驱者的劳作不再赢得敬畏。
的确，如果揭露这一出售计划得以推进的勤勉方式，我们将向那位中国绅士暨真正的体育家致敬，他曾受邀 quietly 支持赞成出售的决议，但在会员大会上，当他迟来地了解到购买者的国籍后，他有勇气明确拒绝履行其角色，因为他的良心反感于一块伟大的运动场地被亵渎的想法。

另一件事
此外，还有一位颇具影响力的体育界中坚人物坚持书面要求，上海跑马总会董事局应在官方行动获得相关会员批准之前，就拟议的转让事宜咨询领事当局，如果这一要求未得到满足，他将毫不犹豫地自行这样做。
但是，现在看来，不幸的是，转让正在走向完成，抵押贷款将被清偿，除了那群感到自己的继承权已被以微不足道的代价出卖的体育人士外，各方都在窃喜自满；他们如今被剥夺了多年来引以为傲的那一优良机构，并确信在上海我们再次看到——即使在体育界——膨胀的暴政也能压制坚实且呼声高昂的少数派的愿望和信念。据报道支付的金额从一百万美元到八十万不等。一位当地评论员声称，欠汇丰银行的款项约为六十万。

一个确凿的迹象
公众所遗忘的事实是，这片1160亩的土地将被日本用作机场，这是永久占领中国大片土地的确凿迹象。此外还有两条道路，是由国际娱乐总会在其 acquired 的土地上修建、铺设沥青，并于几年前移交给中国当局的。
社会大众惋惜匆匆处置了这一巨大的“城市之肺”，体育人士则哀叹其慈善同胞缺乏远见。

D. J. Hau
Rat

The I.R.C. Sale:
Mr. Yu Ya-ching's Protest

To the Editor of the
"NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS"

SIR,—I shall be very much obliged, if you will kindly publish in your valuable column of to-morrow's edition, my attached copy of letter dated June 19, 1938 addressed to The Chairman, General Committee, International Recreation Club.
YU YA-CHING.
Shanghai, June 23.

SIR,—Referring to the sale of the Club's property situated at Kiangwan district I would reiterate that I have evinced my objection before the Shareholders' Meeting held on June 13 1938 and also reaffirmed same in my letter of June 15, 1938 to you, both of which have undoubtedly had your kind attention.
As I am well apprehensive of the traditional facts about the recreation ground at Kiangwan, I am much pleased to sketch, for your guidance, as hereunder:—
About in the end of Ching Dynasty, on account of the fact that Chinese were prohibited to register as Members of the Shanghai Race Club, some of the Chinese in Shanghai felt much indignant with the consequence of organizing the International Recreation Club and setting up Kiangwan race ground. It was through the joint petition of some people and me to General Tern Fang, the Viceroy of Nanking that the official permission was granted to purchase ground from people in Kiangwan at the price of $60 per mow, specially appropriating the said ground for Chinese Racing. The same property was not permitted to be transferred to the foreign consulate registration At that time, among the Members of the International Recreation Club, Mr. B. A. Clarke was the only foreign Member, and all the rest were Chinese. Later on, the big proprietor Mr. Yih Tse-hung, transferred a part of his shares to Shanghai Race Club, thus beginning to have the addition of foreign members gradually. During that period Chinese people, (previous land-owners) basing on the old case, put obstacles in the way, making many protests. I was asked to effect reconciliation. As understanding was reached adjusting that the ground was used for Chinese racing exclusively, and it should never be appropriated for any other use. Therefore, it was for the same reason why the ground was not permitted to be transferred to a foreign consulate registration.
The present proposition of sale is purely for obtaining funds to clear up the debts owing to the Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation. In my opinion, the said bank has no intention to interfere with the sale or not, so far as they could locate their claim to the debtor's property. Now, counting on the wide margin of the assets in excess of the liabilities, this Club should raise funds from other sources to pay the debt. But Shanghai Race Club does not so. I cannot agree to their action.
The original proposition, held at a Committee Meeting of the International Recreation Club on May 17, was purely to confirm and pass the properties owned by the International Recreation Club into the hands of the Stewards of the Shanghai Race Club, in order to give the fullest protection to such properties during the present military operations between China and Japan—The Committee were assured that in this manner they could ask and would receive the assistance of the H.B.M. Consular Authorities.
There was no mention at such original Meeting that the properties would be put on the market for sale —nor was there any intention from the Club's Bankers Messrs. The Hongkong & Shanghai Banking Corporation that they were making any serious demand for the repayment of the Club's indebtedness to them, and that this was only a formal demand.
In the meanwhile, unknown to The Chairman and Committee of the International Recreation Club, the steward of the Shanghai Race Club had been negotiating for the sale of the property to Japanese buyers—and this only became known to the Chairman and Committee of the International Club at a Committee Meeting held on May 25—and, from thence onward—difficulties did arise, as the Chairman and Committee of the International Recreation Club could not support such a proposition which eventually developed into the Extraordinary Meeting held at the Shanghai Race Club on June 13—at which the Stewards of the Shanghai Race Club acted contrary to the wishes of the Committee of the International Recreation Club and used their preponderance of votes in order to carry the issue.
As I have known quite well about the history of Kiangwan Race Course and have in fact undergone the experience of it, I presume that should the sale become realised, there would happen complication as to the old case in future, although many previous land owners of this locality leave Shanghai at present. Those who made the proposal of sale should be held responsible. I write this letter to request your kind attention and through your goodself to ask the Members of Shanghai Race Club to give careful consideration of the above facts.
Sgd. YU YA-CHING.
Shanghai, June 19.

A. C. Hall
（签名）

国际娱乐总会出售案：
虞洽卿先生的抗议

致《字林西报》编辑先生

先生，——如蒙贵报在明日版面的宝贵专栏中刊登我附上的、于1938年6月19日致国际娱乐总会总委员会主席的信函副本，我将不胜感激。
虞洽卿。
上海，6月23日。

先生，——关于位于江湾地区的总会产业出售一事，我重申我曾在1938年6月13日举行的股东会议上表示反对，并在1938年6月15日致阁下的信中再次确认了这一点，这两点无疑已得到阁下的关注。
由于我对江湾游乐场的历史事实深感忧虑，我很高兴在此简述如下，以供阁下参考：——
大约在清朝末年，鉴于华人被禁止注册成为上海跑马总会的会员，上海部分华人对此感到愤慨，遂组织成立了国际娱乐总会，并建立了江湾赛马场。正是通过我和其他人向两江总督端方将军的联合请愿，才获官方许可，以每亩60元的价格从江湾民众手中购买土地，专门将该地块用于华人赛马。该产业当时不允许过户至外国领事馆注册。那时，在国际娱乐总会的会员中，B. A. Clarke 先生是唯一的外籍会员，其余均为华人。后来，大业主叶子衡先生将其部分股份转让给上海跑马总会，从而开始逐渐增加外籍会员。在此期间，华人（即原土地所有者）依据旧案设置障碍，提出许多抗议。我被请求进行调解。最终达成谅解，调整规定该地块专用于华人赛马，绝不得挪作他用。因此，这也是该地块不被允许过户至外国领事馆注册的原因。
目前的出售提议纯粹是为了筹集资金，以清偿欠汇丰银行的债务。在我看来，只要该银行能对其债务人的财产主张债权，它并无意干涉出售与否。现在，考虑到资产远超负债的宽裕幅度，本总会应从其他来源筹集资金以偿还债务。但上海跑马总会并未如此行事。我无法同意他们的做法。
最初的提议是在5月17日国际娱乐总会委员会会议上提出的，纯粹是为了确认并将国际娱乐总会拥有的财产移交给上海跑马总会的董事们保管，以便在中日目前的军事行动期间对这些财产提供最充分的保护——委员会确信，通过这种方式，他们可以请求并获得英国驻华领事当局的支持。
在那次最初的会议上，没有提及将财产投放市场出售——总会的银行家汇丰银行也没有认真要求偿还总会对他们的欠款，那只是一项形式上的要求。
与此同时，在国际娱乐总会主席和委员会不知情的情况下，上海跑马总会的董事一直在与日本买家谈判出售该财产——直到5月25日举行的委员会会议上，国际俱乐部的主席和委员会才得知此事——从此以后，困难确实出现了，因为国际娱乐总会的主席和委员会无法支持这一提议，这最终导致于6月13日在上海跑马总会召开特别会议——在该会议上，上海跑马总会的董事们违背了国际娱乐总会委员会的意愿，利用其票数优势通过了该议题。
由于我非常了解江湾赛马场的历史，并且实际上有过相关经历，我推测，如果出售成为现实，尽管该地区以前的许多土地所有者目前不在上海，未来仍会就旧案发生纠纷。提出出售建议的人应承担责任。我写此信是恳请阁下关注，并通过阁下请上海跑马总会的会员仔细考虑上述事实。
签名：虞洽卿。
上海，6月19日。

A. C. Hall
（签名）

MR. YU YA-CHING OPPOSES THE SALE OF KIANGWAN RACE COURSE

Mr. Yu Ya-ching ( 虞洽卿 ) is one of the Directors of the former International Recreation Club. On June 23, he sent the following letter to the Chairman of the General Affairs Committee of the International Recreation Club opposing the sale of the Kiangwan Race Course to the Japanese :-
"At the close of the Tsing Dynasty, a section of the Chinese people, who were angered at the Shanghai Race Club because it had refused to allow Chinese to become members, formed the International Recreation Club and requested the Viceroy at Nanking to allow it to construct a race course and that this course should not be sold to foreigners. At first, there was only one foreigner connected with the Recreation Club, but the number was later increased.
"The object of selling the Kiangwan Race Course is to secure funds to pay the Hongkong & Shanghai Banking Corporation. In my opinion, the bank never had any intention to interfere, whether this property be sold or not. From the fact that the value of the property is greater than the amount owing, it seems to me that the International Recreation Club should have repaid the loan by some other means.
"The General Affairs Committee held a meeting on May 17 with the object of handing over the property to the Shanghai Race Club to be held in safe custody so as to avoid loss during the Sino-Japanese hostilities. No mention was made during the meeting about the sale of the property. Furthermore, the Hongkong Bank was not pressing for payment. Officers of the Shanghai Race Club opened negotiations with the Japanese for the sale of the Kiangwan Race Course without first securing the approval of the Chairman of the Committee of the International Recreation Club and the Chairman knew of it only when it was holding a meeting on May 25. Trouble arose because the Chairman and the members of the Committee did not approve of the sale. As a result, an extraordinary meeting was held at the Shanghai Race Club on June 13, at which officers of the Shanghai Race Club approved the sale, contrary to the views of the Committee of the International Recreation Club.
"I have full details regarding the history of the Kiangwan Race Course. Most of the land-owners of the course are not in Shanghai and difficulties will arise in future should the sale materialize. The persons who had proposed the sale of the property will be held responsible."

D.S. Hial

虞洽卿先生反对出售江湾赛马场

虞洽卿先生（虞洽卿）是前国际娱乐总会的董事之一。6月23日，他致信国际娱乐总会总务委员会主席，反对将江湾赛马场出售给日本人：-
“在清朝末年，一部分华人因上海跑马总会拒绝允许华人成为会员而感到愤怒，于是成立了国际娱乐总会，并请求南京总督允许其建造赛马场，且该赛马场不得出售给外国人。起初，与娱乐总会有关联的外国人只有一名，但后来人数增加了。
“出售江湾赛马场的目的是筹集资金以偿还汇丰银行。在我看来，无论该财产是否出售，银行都无意干涉。从财产价值大于欠款金额这一事实来看，我认为国际娱乐总会本应通过其他方式偿还贷款。
“总务委员会于5月17日召开会议，目的是将财产移交给上海跑马总会妥善保管，以避免在中日敌对行动期间遭受损失。会议期间未提及出售财产之事。此外，汇丰银行并未催款。上海跑马总会的官员在未先获得国际娱乐总会委员会主席批准的情况下，就与日本人展开谈判，欲出售江湾赛马场，而主席直到5月25日开会时才知道此事。麻烦由此产生，因为主席和委员会成员不赞成出售。结果，6月13日在上海跑马总会召开了一次特别会议，上海跑马总会的官员在会上批准了出售，这与国际娱乐总会委员会的观点相左。
“我掌握有关江湾赛马场历史的详细资料。赛马场的大部分土地所有者不在上海，如果出售成真，未来将出现困难。提出出售该财产的人将被追究责任。”

D.S. Hial
Q. 3%
